A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same multiscale GNN training work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material across the expanded and renumbered appendices.

before.justification: v3 reports original classification and segmentation experiments, computational costs, timings, and supplementary analyses in Section 6 and Appendices B–G.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds molecular graph-classification results, memory measurements, and sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: The three training strategies, Algorithms 1–2, Equation (5), and pooling options are retained. Appendix C presents Algorithms 3–5 as implementation details of existing coarsening procedures; it does not establish a new training method.

E1.justification: v4 adds NCI1 and ogbg-molhiv in Appendix I, extending evaluation to molecular graph classification. This substantially broadens task coverage beyond the retained node-classification and segmentation experiments; the existing datasets remain.

E2.justification: Unlike v3's comparisons primarily against full-graph training, v4 Table 19 adds a Flickr comparison with GraphSAGE, FastGCN, S-GCN, AS-GCN, ClusterGCN, and four GraphSAINT variants. These are reported comparisons using published baseline scores attributed to Zeng et al. (2020), not documented baseline reruns.

E3.justification: Existing experimental settings remain unchanged. Added evaluations specify two-level GCN training for molecular classification, accuracy for NCI1, AUC-ROC for MolHIV, and Micro-F1 for the new Flickr comparison. Appendix J adds controlled PubMed experiments varying coarsening ratios and epoch allocation.

E4.justification: v4 adds empirical checks of the loss-discrepancy factors gamma_r (Table 8), memory profiling across architectures and coarsening levels (Table 9), and PubMed sensitivity studies of coarsening ratios and epoch schedules (Tables 27–28). These substantially extend the retained motivating examples and convergence analysis.

E5.justification: The retained experiments keep their three-seed and standard-deviation reporting. Added accuracy tables use the existing parenthetical dispersion format; no increased run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or new statistical estimation procedure are documented.

E6.justification: Matched existing result tables retain their numerical values. v4 adds results in Tables 8, 9, 19, and 26–28, including NCI1 accuracy of 70.45% for random coarsening versus 69.37% for full-graph training, and MolHIV AUC-ROC of 71.01% for hybrid coarsening versus 70.39%. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over corresponding v3 experiments.

T1.justification: The linear sketching bound and Appendix A proof are retained, with notation revised and epsilon positivity made explicit. However, v4 Equation (10) removes v3's ellipsis representing intermediate scales, leaving the displayed general-R expansion incomplete. This is a limited mathematical regression.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contributions remain essentially unchanged. The conclusion qualifies the previous claim of improvements across all considered settings by specifying that at least one coarsening method improves performance for each dataset/network combination.

C2.justification: New Section 7 explicitly acknowledges that the full graph must still fit in memory, that variant selection lacks a principled criterion, and that some settings exhibit high variance. Appendix J also explains the efficiency-versus-coarsening tradeoff and the preference for allocating more epochs to cheaper coarse levels.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code-repository pointer in Section 1 and coarsening pseudocode in Appendix C; existing setup tables are retained. The new documentation contains inconsistencies: m is described as a ratio but used as a node count, and the adjacency-power loop conflicts with Equation (5).

R1.justification: v4 adds discussion or citations concerning multiscale CNN training, ClusterGCN, NCI1, and informative graph benchmarks through Ahamed et al., Chiang et al., Wale et al., and Coupette et al. The broader research positioning remains stable. The additional GraphSAINT bibliography entry represents an already cited work.

P1.justification: Localized edits consolidate the introductory contribution discussion, expand dataset descriptions, standardize citations, and add Limitations and Acknowledgements sections. Appendix headings and affiliations are updated, while most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 substantially expands the displays with six new tables—8, 9, 19, and 26–28—and three algorithm panels. Figures 1–5 are retained, while existing tables are redistributed and renumbered within the publication layout.

improvement.justification: The added assumption checks, sensitivity studies, graph-classification evidence, and explicit full-graph memory limitation make v4's design choices and applicability easier to assess. The gains are limited by underspecified new comparison protocols, missing memory units in Table 9, and new equation/pseudocode inconsistencies. The central methods, existing results, and proof otherwise remain stable.
